provenance_note: MIXED, AND EVERY FILE SAYS WHICH IT IS. Entries in `fixtures` are SYNTHETIC unless listed in `captured`: hand-built to the shapes and behaviours the Phase 0 acceptance test measured across 117 live requests, so the rules they exercise are real even though the bytes are not. Entries in `captured` are verbatim provider bytes, the tier `providers/fixtures/record.py` reserves for capture_live(). SPRINT 5B ADDED THE FIRST CAPTURED BALLDONTLIE PAYLOAD, and doing so showed why the distinction is not bookkeeping: the synthetic play corpus had been built against a schema the live API does not emit (`type`, `game_id`, `clock` for `type_slug`, a nested `game`, `clock_display`), against a play-type vocabulary the API does not use, and against first-down text the API never writes. Every classifier certified against it was certified against fiction. A synthetic fixture answers whatever it was written to answer; only a captured one can contradict its author.
subject_ids_are_real: Player and team identifiers are the REAL BALLDONTLIE ids recorded in providers/fixtures/wp1_identity/bdl_subjects_2025_w17.json, so a subject key produced from a stat row here can be matched against WP1's identity directory rather than against a second set of invented ids. Two exceptions are marked synthetic in the builder: the two kicker participant ids in the play stream, which WP1's corpus does not need.
statistics_are_invented: Every FIGURE is invented. These files assert nothing about what any player actually did in 2025 week 17, and no reconciliation reads them.

fixtures.fantasy_weekly_stats__per_page-100__seas: fantasy/weekly_stats, two pages. Exercises 0F-1 zero omission, 0F-2 the empty stats block, 0F-16 the PK spelling and the stray DT, 0F-17 the null-player DST row, and cursor pagination.
fixtures.games__per_page-100__seasons-2025__weeks: games for week 1 WITHOUT a postseason filter — the naive query. Exercises 0F-14 the postseason week collision, 0F-4 null quarter scores, and an unfinished game that has no score to read.
fixtures.plays__game_ids-424186__per_page-100.jso: plays for one game. Exercises 0F-5 scrambled order and non-monotonic ids, 0F-6 the null team, 0F-7 possession inversion, 0F-8 participant attribution, 0F-9 both blocked-kick slugs, 0F-12 the pick six, 0F-13 stat_yardage disagreeing with the text, and a record after end-of-game.
fixtures.fantasy_projections__per_page-100__seaso: fantasy/projections, two pages (Sprint 2B). Exercises the projection block as Phase 0 measured it: the weekly_stats vocabulary plus yardage and points-allowed BUCKET probabilities, `receptions` ABSENT so a PPR input must be derived from `targets`, kicker distance modelling, a null-player DST row, and a `collected_at` freshness stamp — which is what snapshot selection orders on. One representative subject per fantasy position: QB, RB, WR, TE, K, DST.
fixtures.plays__game_id-7005__per_page-100__CAPTU: CAPTURED. Verbatim /plays response for a real 2024 game — see `captured` for provenance. Exercises the live `type_slug` vocabulary, `end_down` as the only first-down signal, the takeaway possession inversion, turnover-on-downs as a team flip with no slug of its own, and a real pick-six attributed to its passer.

sprint_2b_note: The projections fixture is SYNTHETIC on the same terms as the rest of this corpus. It is a FORECAST fixture, not a result fixture: the two share one vocabulary and must never share one meaning, which is why a stored snapshot records the endpoint it came from.
